request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change and all 4 Playwright tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V31__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table. Each hold has a from-date and an optional to-date, the to-date can't be before the from-date, and a person can have any number of holds. It drops the old yes/no `held` column.
- **Which claims are left out:** a claim is now left out of the live totals only when it is OPEN, isn't bound by a statement, and is dated within one of the person's holds. All other claims count as before. The same rule applies everywhere totals are worked out: the person's figures, the sheet totals, statements and closing a period.
- **Holding:** adding a hold takes a from-date (blank means the sheet's today) and an optional to-date. It writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=… from=<date>`, and the totals are recorded again only when they actually move. If the to-date is before the from-date, the hold is refused and nothing is saved or written to the audit file.
- **Release is gone:** there is no release action and no `PERSON_RELEASED` record any more. A hold simply ends on its to-date.
- **Screen:** each person's row lists their holds (`person-hold-line`) and has from/to date fields with a Hold button. `person-hold` shows yes when the person has any hold, whatever its dates. The period totals on screen use the same rule as the server.

**Choices you may want to revisit**
- **PENDING claims now always count.** The request says only OPEN claims are left out, so I followed it literally. Before, holding someone also left out their PENDING claims.
- **Existing held people:** anyone already on hold is moved to an open-ended hold starting at their earliest claim's date (or the sheet's today if they have no claims). That keeps all their unbound OPEN claims out of the totals; claims a statement had bound now count. The database is in-memory and reset on each start, so this only matters if the app later uses a lasting database.
- **A future hold shows yes:** because `person-hold` means "has any hold", someone whose only hold starts next month already shows yes.

The main changes are in `Dues.java`, `Person.java` (with a new `HoldSpan.java`), `PersonService.java`, `PersonController.java` and `people.ts`.
